findings.description: The reports bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so stored objects are not guaranteed to be encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key. Sensitive report data would be stored without explicit encryption controls.
No ACL is specified and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is attached, leaving the bucket without explicit controls against public ACLs or bucket policies granting anonymous access.
The bucket has no logging block, so object-level access to archived reports leaves no S3 server access audit trail, impeding detection and investigation of unauthorized access.
Versioning is not enabled and force_destroy is true, so objects can be overwritten or permanently deleted with no recovery, enabling destructive tampering of archived data.
The ledger export bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so financial export data is stored without enforced KMS encryption at rest.
No logging block is configured for the ledger bucket, so reads and writes to sensitive financial exports are not recorded for audit.
Versioning is disabled while force_destroy is true, so ledger export objects can be silently overwritten or destroyed without recovery.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so a later ACL or bucket policy change could expose financial data publicly without a guardrail.
The model artifacts bucket lacks server_side_encryption_configuration, so artifacts are stored without enforced encryption at rest under a managed key.
No public access block is configured, leaving no account-level guardrail preventing public ACLs or policies on this bucket.

The runbooks bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration; operational runbooks frequently contain sensitive procedural and connection details and are stored unencrypted by explicit configuration.
No logging block is configured, so access to operational runbooks is not auditable via S3 server access logs.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block guards this bucket against future public ACL or policy grants.

The audit log destination bucket sets force_destroy = true, allowing all audit logs to be deleted along with the bucket, and has no public access block, weakening the integrity and confidentiality of the audit trail.

findings.issue_category: missing access logging on log bucket
findings.description: The central audit bucket itself has no access logging configured, so tampering with or exfiltration of stored logs is not recorded.

A vendor roster spreadsheet is uploaded from the repository into a bucket that has no default encryption, and no server_side_encryption or kms_key_id is set on the object; potentially sensitive vendor data is committed to source control and stored unencrypted.
